seo.title: Smart Contract Deployment Checklist
seo.description: Pre-mainnet deployment checklist for Solidity smart contracts. Covers testing, configuration, access control, and production monitoring.

content.intro: The definitive pre-deployment checklist for Solidity developers. From final code review to mainnet deployment, this guide ensures nothing is missed when real money is on the line.

sections.heading: Final Code Review
sections.description: Last checks before freezing the code.

items.title: All tests passing with 100% of critical paths covered
items.description: Run full test suite. Ensure all edge cases for value transfers and state changes are tested.

items.title: Remove all console.log and debug code
items.description: Search for console.log, hardhat/console.sol imports, and test-only functions.

items.title: Verify correct Solidity version
items.description: Use a stable, audited compiler version. Avoid floating pragmas (^0.8.0).

items.title: Check optimizer settings
items.description: Document optimizer runs. Higher runs = cheaper execution, larger bytecode.

items.title: Verify contract sizes under 24KB
items.description: Check bytecode size limits. Split contracts or use libraries if needed.

items.title: Remove unused imports and dead code
items.description: Clean up any code that isn't used in production paths.

items.title: Verify NatSpec documentation is complete
items.description: All public/external functions should have @notice, @param, and @return docs.

items.title: Confirm audit findings are resolved
items.description: All critical and high findings must be fixed. Medium issues should be addressed or documented.

sections.heading: Configuration & Parameters
sections.description: Verify all deployment parameters are correct.

items.title: Verify constructor arguments
items.description: Double-check all addresses, rates, and configuration values. Use checksummed addresses.

items.title: Confirm admin/owner addresses
items.description: Owner should be a multisig, not an EOA. Verify multisig signers and threshold.

items.title: Set appropriate timelock delays
items.description: Critical operations should have 24-48 hour timelocks minimum.

items.title: Verify oracle addresses and feeds
items.description: Confirm Chainlink feed addresses are correct for target network.

items.title: Check fee parameters and limits
items.description: Verify fee percentages, max fees, and fee recipient addresses.

items.title: Confirm token addresses and decimals
items.description: Verify all token addresses. Check decimals handling for non-18 decimal tokens.

items.title: Set initial rate limits
items.description: Configure conservative limits for withdrawals, mints, and other operations.

items.title: Document all magic numbers
items.description: Every constant should be documented with its meaning and rationale.

items.title: Deploy multisig wallet first
items.description: Create Safe or other multisig with appropriate signers before contract deployment.

items.title: Set up role-based access control
items.description: Grant roles to appropriate addresses. Use principle of least privilege.

items.title: Configure timelock controller
items.description: Deploy timelock and set as admin for upgradeable contracts.

items.title: Verify emergency admin setup
items.description: Emergency pause should be accessible quickly but protected from abuse.

items.title: Document all privileged addresses
items.description: Create public documentation of all admin addresses and their capabilities.

items.title: Set up monitoring for admin actions
items.description: Configure alerts for all privileged transactions.

items.title: Plan key rotation procedure
items.description: Document how to rotate keys if a signer is compromised.

items.title: Renounce deployer privileges
items.description: Transfer ownership and renounce any deployer-specific roles after setup.

items.title: Deploy to testnet with production config
items.description: Use identical constructor args and deployment scripts as mainnet.

items.title: Run integration tests against testnet
items.description: Execute full user flows against deployed testnet contracts.

items.title: Test upgrade path on testnet
items.description: If upgradeable, test the full upgrade process including storage migration.

items.title: Verify with block explorer
items.description: Confirm contract verification works and ABI is correct.

items.title: Test emergency procedures
items.description: Execute pause, emergency withdrawal, and circuit breaker functions.

items.title: Test frontend integration
items.description: Verify dapp works correctly with testnet deployment.

items.title: Measure gas costs
items.description: Record gas usage for all major operations. Optimize if needed.

items.title: Test with realistic data
items.description: Simulate production-like conditions including high volumes.

items.title: Choose optimal deployment time
items.description: Deploy during low gas periods. Avoid weekends for critical infrastructure.

items.title: Prepare deployment wallet with ETH
items.description: Fund deployer with 2-3x expected gas costs. Use fresh wallet.

items.title: Execute deployment script
items.description: Run automated deployment. Never deploy manually transaction by transaction.

items.title: Verify all contracts on Etherscan
items.description: Submit source code verification immediately after deployment.

items.title: Record all deployed addresses
items.description: Document every contract address, transaction hash, and block number.

items.title: Verify initialization state
items.description: Check all storage variables are correctly initialized.

items.title: Execute post-deployment configuration
items.description: Set up any remaining parameters that couldn't be set in constructor.

items.title: Transfer ownership to multisig
items.description: Move admin rights from deployer to production multisig.

items.title: Execute smoke tests on mainnet
items.description: Run basic operations with small amounts to verify functionality.

items.title: Verify contract ownership
items.description: Confirm owner/admin is the intended multisig address.

items.title: Check oracle connections
items.description: Verify price feeds are returning correct, fresh data.

items.title: Test pause functionality
items.description: Verify pause works and can be triggered by guardian.

items.title: Verify event emissions
items.description: Confirm events are emitting correctly for indexers.

items.title: Check subgraph indexing
items.description: Verify The Graph or other indexers are picking up events.

items.title: Test frontend with production contracts
items.description: Full end-to-end test of dapp with real mainnet contracts.

items.title: Document deployment in changelog
items.description: Record deployment details, addresses, and any issues encountered.

items.title: Configure transaction monitoring
items.description: Set up Tenderly, OpenZeppelin Defender, or similar for tx monitoring.

items.title: Set up balance alerts
items.description: Alert on unusual balance changes or large withdrawals.

items.title: Monitor for failed transactions
items.description: Alert on reverted transactions, especially privileged operations.

items.title: Set up oracle health monitoring
items.description: Alert on stale prices or oracle deviations.

items.title: Configure invariant monitoring
items.description: Set up Forta bots or custom monitoring for protocol invariants.

items.title: Create incident response runbook
items.description: Document steps for common incidents: pause, upgrade, fund recovery.

items.title: Set up on-call rotation
items.description: Ensure someone can respond to alerts 24/7.

items.title: Schedule regular security reviews
items.description: Plan periodic audits and security assessments.

proTips: Use deterministic deployments: CREATE2 lets you predict addresses and deploy to the same address across chains.
Always deploy from scripts, never manually: Manual deployments lead to configuration errors. Automated scripts are repeatable and auditable.
Keep deployment private keys offline: Use hardware wallets for deployment. Never store deployer keys on servers.
Deploy during low-activity periods: Tuesday-Thursday, outside US and Asian market hours, typically has lowest gas.
Have a rollback plan: Know exactly what to do if deployment fails halfway. Document recovery steps before starting.
